notes.claim: Connected in a string, all cells receive the same charge current, so controlling each cell's voltage as it reaches full is almost impossible.
On discharge the weak cell holds less capacity and empties first, and a high load can push it into reverse polarity.
On charge the weak cell reaches full first and goes into heat-generating overcharge while the strong cells still accept charge.

On float, one maker allows each vented cell to sit 0.05 V below to 0.10 V above the per-cell float voltage, while the battery's total stays within its limits, so a good total can hide a cell outside that band (added for i6's float view).
Parallel strings should be of the same capacity, design and age, at most four, with cables of equal resistance in each string, the same cross-section and length (added for i6's parallel card).
A weak cell driven into reverse under load can be stressed until it develops a permanent short.
On float, weak cells may overcharge while strong cells stay starved, and a float current too high for the faded cell may leave its strong neighbours undercharged and sulphating.
A charge may cover a weak cell for a while, but the flaw is likely to show again within hours because the faulty cell self-discharges fast.
Cell mismatch is a common cause of failure in industrial batteries.
An equalising charge is called for when cells differ by more than about 0.10 V, or by more than 10 points (0.010) of specific gravity (added for i6's practice list).
Cells 40 points of specific gravity apart are a performance problem, and the cell is considered defective (added for i6's practice list).

sources.title: Battery University | BU-803a: Cell Matching and Balancing
sources.quote: The weak cell holds less capacity and is discharged more quickly than their strong brothers.

sources.title: Battery University | BU-803a: Cell Matching and Balancing
sources.quote: Going empty first causes their strong brothers to overrun their feeble sibling to the point where a high load can push the weak cell into reverse polarity.

sources.title: Battery University | BU-803a: Cell Matching and Balancing
sources.quote: On charge, the weak cell reaches full charge first, and then goes into heat-generating overcharge, while the strong brothers still accept charge and stay cool.

sources.title: Bu 403 Charging Lead Acid — Battery University
sources.quote: Connected in a string, all cells receive the same charge current and controlling individual cell voltages as each reaches full capacity is almost impossible.

sources.title: Flooded Stationary Lead Acid Batteries IOM — EnerSys
sources.quote: Deviations of individual cell voltages of –0.05 to +0.10 V/c may be observed. However the total voltage of the battery shall be within the limits stated above.

sources.title: Flooded Stationary Lead Acid Batteries IOM — EnerSys
sources.quote: In the case of parallel connected strings use batteries of the same capacity, design and age only with a maximum of 4 parallel strings. The resistance of the cables in each string must be the same, e.g. same cross-section, same length.

sources.title: Bu 502 Discharging At High And Low Temperatures — Battery University
sources.quote: Known as cell reversal, the weak cell gets stressed to the point of developing a permanent electrical short.

sources.title: Bu 403 Charging Lead Acid — Battery University
sources.quote: Weak cells may go into overcharge while strong cells remain in a starved state. A float current that is too high for the faded cell might sulfate the strong neighbor due to undercharge.

sources.title: Battery University | BU-803a: Cell Matching and Balancing
sources.quote: A charge may temporarily cover the deficiency, but the flaw will likely resurface again after a few hours due to the high self-discharge of the faulty cell.

sources.title: Battery University | BU-803a: Cell Matching and Balancing
sources.quote: Cell mismatch is a common cause of failure in industrial batteries.

sources.title: Battery University | BU-803a: Cell Matching and Balancing
sources.quote: Manufacturers of golf cars, aerial work platforms, floor scrubbers and other battery-powered vehicles recommend an equalizing charge if the voltage difference between the cells is greater than +/– 0.10V, or if the specific gravity varies more than 10 points (0.010 on the SG scale).

sources.title: Battery University | BU-803a: Cell Matching and Balancing
sources.quote: A difference in specific gravity of 40 points poses a performance problem and the cell is considered defective.
